problem: The comparison sign has dropped out: the text reads "ΔG  0 means the forward reaction does not go; the reverse does." With no symbol, a student cannot tell which sign is being described. The criterion for the spontaneous case (ΔG < 0) is also missing entirely.
fix: ΔG < 0 means the forward reaction goes; ΔG > 0 means the forward reaction does not go and the reverse does. At ΔG = 0 the system is at equilibrium.

problem: The value of RT/F at 298 K is not 0.0592 V. RT/F = 8.314 × 298 ÷ 96500 = 0.0257 V. The factor 0.0592 V is 2.303RT/F, i.e. the value after converting ln to log₁₀.
The chapter gives ΔG < 0 and ΔG > 0 but never states the equilibrium condition, so the link between ΔG and K = 1 is left implicit.
fix: Add: ΔG = 0 means the system is at equilibrium; for standard conditions this gives K = 1 when ΔG° = 0.

problem: "Heat capacity is C = q/ΔT, in J K⁻¹" does not say which heat capacity it is, and most reactions here are at constant pressure, where the useful quantity is C_p.
fix: Heat capacity is C = q/ΔT, in J K⁻¹; at constant pressure the heat absorbed is q_p = C_p ΔT, so C_p = ΔH/ΔT.
